---
title: "Install Record"
---

Quarto Wizard writes a file named `.quarto-source.yml` in the folder of each extension that it installs.
This file is the install record.
It says where the extension came from, and it holds a checksum of each installed file.

## Shared with Quarto 2

Quarto 2 writes and reads the same file.
You can install an extension with Quarto Wizard and update it with Quarto 2, or the other way round.
Each tool finds the source in the record and checks the files against the checksums.

Do not edit the file by hand.
Quarto Wizard and Quarto 2 both write it.

## What the Record Holds

The record holds these items:

- The source that you installed from, for example `owner/repository@v1.2.0`.
- The type of the source: GitHub, URL, local folder or local archive.
- For a GitHub source, the update source, under the `quarto-wizard` key: `track`, and the full `commit` in some cases.
- A checksum for each file of the extension.

The Extensions Installed view reads the source from the record.
It uses the source to check for updates, to reinstall the extension, and to open the source.

An extension that has no record can still have `source` and `source-type` keys in its `_extension.yml` file.
This is the format of Quarto Wizard 3.
Quarto Wizard still reads these keys.
The next update of the extension writes a record.

## The Update Source

A GitHub extension follows one of two update sources:

- `tag`: the latest version tag of the repository.
  This is the default.
- `branch`: the latest commit of a branch.
  This is the default branch, unless the source names a branch.

Quarto Wizard saves the choice as `quarto-wizard.track` in the record.
An update follows the saved value, and not the current setting.
The `@ref` in the source only says where the files came from.
It never stops an update.

The `commit` item is the full 40-character commit, in lower case.
The Extensions Installed view shows the first seven characters.
Quarto 2 ignores the `quarto-wizard` key.

This table shows what a GitHub install records:

| Case                                       | `source`             | `track`  | `commit`    |
| ------------------------------------------ | -------------------- | -------- | ----------- |
| Tag mode, latest tag `v1.4.0`              | `owner/repo@v1.4.0`  | `tag`    | none        |
| Branch mode, default branch                | `owner/repo`         | `branch` | full commit |
| Branch `dev`                               | `owner/repo@dev`     | `branch` | full commit |
| Tag `v1.2.0`                               | `owner/repo@v1.2.0`  | `tag`    | none        |
| Commit `abc1234`                           | `owner/repo@abc1234` | `tag`    | none        |
| Tag mode, no version tag in the repository | `owner/repo`         | `tag`    | full commit |

A commit has nothing to follow, so the next update of an extension that you installed from a commit goes to the latest tag.
If a repository has no version tag, tag mode installs the head of the default branch.
Update then compares commits until the repository has a version tag.
An extension from a subdirectory (`owner/repo/subdirectory@ref`) follows the same table.

A record that has no `track` item, for example a record that Quarto 2 wrote, counts as `tag`.
An extension that has no record also counts as `tag`.
A URL source, a local folder and a local archive have no update source.

To change the update source of an installed extension, use **Change Update Source** in the Extensions Installed view.
To set the update source of new installs, use the `quartoWizard.install.updateSource` setting.
See [Configuration](configuration.qmd).

## Local Changes Are Detected

Before Quarto Wizard replaces an extension, it compares the files with the checksums in the record.
A file that you changed, removed or added counts as a local change.

If the extension has local changes, Quarto Wizard does not replace it.
It shows a warning that lists the files, at most ten.
If more files differ, the warning ends with `and <n> more`.

The warning has two actions:

- **Replace anyway** replaces the extension and removes your changes.
- **Cancel** writes nothing.

If you close the warning, Quarto Wizard also writes nothing.

**Update All** never replaces an extension that has local changes.
It skips the extension, updates the others, and shows one message that lists each skipped extension and its files.
The output log has the same list.

An extension that has no record has no checksums.
Quarto Wizard replaces it after the usual confirmation, and writes a record.
It then tells you that it could not check the extension for local changes.

## Install the Same Version Again

If the installed extension is already at the version that you install, Quarto Wizard writes nothing.
It shows the message `<extension> is already at version <version>.`
This is also true when you changed files of the extension.

**Update** and **Update All** replace the extension at the same version, because a new tag or commit can keep the version.
If the extension has local changes, **Update** shows the warning and **Update All** skips the extension.

An extension that has no record is also left as it is at the same version.
To give it a record, remove the extension, then install it again.

To reset an extension to its original files, use **Reinstall Extension** in the Extensions Installed view.
Reinstall replaces the extension even when it is at the same version.
Reinstall keeps the update source of the extension.
The record tells Reinstall what to install:

- In tag mode, Reinstall installs the recorded tag again.
- In branch mode, Reinstall installs the recorded commit again.
  The extension keeps following the branch.
- If the record has no tag and no commit, Reinstall installs the latest tag.
  This version can be newer than the installed version.

If the extension has local changes, Reinstall first shows the warning with **Replace anyway** and **Cancel**.
